Unfortunately "Jackson" is a very common name so it is extremely difficult to connect some of these earlier people conclusively. I have concentrated on Sussex County records since I believe that my earliest ancestors came from there. The earliest JACKSON I have found in Delaware was Cornelius Jackson who appeared in Lewes DE in 1681. For the earliest mixed-race Jacksons we must look at the records of St. George's Chapel and the Lewes/Cool Springs Presbyterian Church in Sussex County where we find that: Jno Jackson , a "mulatto", baptised his son William Jackson at St. Georges Chapel on June 15,1746 and also recorded the birth of his daughter Patience Jackson , born on 25 October 1748. The Lewes/Cool Springs records mention that Patience later married Job Friend, a mulatto, at the home of Mr. McIlvain on 8 June, 1772 William Jackson and his wife Nelly, recorded the birth of their daughter Lydia at St. George's. Lydia was born 19 October, 1768 and baptised 20 August, 1769. William was called a mulatto in the records. William appears in the 1773 and 1774 Indian River Hundred taxables. He's listed in the 1810 and 1820 Nanticoke Hundred census records as head of a "free colored" household of 4. Annanias Jackson and his wife Hester registered the birth of their daughter Hester at St. George's on 10 March 1785. No mention is made of race in these documents but the 1810 DE census records list an "Annias Jackson" as head of a household of 8 free colored persons in Indian River Hundred. Per the Lewes/Cool Springs records, Agnes Jackson married Edward Harmon on Nov. 27, 1788, Isreal Jackson married Polly Handsor on Aug. 29, 1802, Hester Jackson married Eli Hitchins on Sept. 9, 1802, and Katherine Jackson married Thomas Hanzor on Feb. 4, 1808. James Jackson , a "Poore Muloto & Several in his family" was a deliquent taxable in Indian River Hundred in 1789. He also appears in the 1810 and 1820 census records for Indian River Hundred, listed as "free colored" Stephen Jackson appears in the Indian River taxables from 1773 - 1784. He's also listed in the 1810 and 1820 Dagsboro Hundred census records as "free colored". From this we can say that: John Jackson was the father of William Jackson & Patience Jackson William Jackson was the father of Lydia Jackson Annanias Jackson was the father of Hester Jackson James, Stephen and Annanias were POSSIBLY children of the original John Jackson The recorded marriages to Handsor, Hitchins and Harmon - names that appear among the current mixed raced community- indicates that as early at the mid 18th century Jacksons were a part of the mixed race Indian community in Sussex County, DE. Unfortunately "Jackson" is a very common name so it is extremely difficult to connect some of these earlier people conclusively. I have concentrated on Sussex County records since I believe that my earliest ancestors came from there.
The earliest JACKSON I have found in Delaware was Cornelius Jackson who appeared in Lewes DE in 
1681
.

For the earliest mixed-race Jacksons we must look at the records of St. George's Chapel and the Lewes/Cool Springs Presbyterian Church  in Sussex County where we find that:


  Jno Jackson , a "mulatto", baptised his son  William Jackson at St. Georges
		Chapel on June 15,
1746
 and also recorded the birth of his daughter  Patience Jackson , born on 
25 		October 1748
. The Lewes/Cool Springs records mention that Patience later married Job Friend, a mulatto, at 		the home of Mr. McIlvain on 8 June, 
1772
 
  William Jackson  and his wife Nelly, recorded the birth of their daughter
		 Lydia  at St. George's. Lydia was born 19 October, 
1768
 and baptised 20 August, 
1769
. William was
		called a mulatto in the records. 

		William appears in the 
1773
 and 
1774
 Indian River Hundred taxables. He's listed in the 
1810
 and
		
1820
 Nanticoke Hundred census records as head of a "free colored" household of 4. 
  Annanias Jackson  and his wife Hester registered the birth of their daughter  Hester
		at St. George's on 
10 March 1785
.  No mention is made of race in these documents but the 
1810
 DE census 		records list an "Annias Jackson" as head of a household of 8 free colored persons in Indian River Hundred. 
	Per the Lewes/Cool Springs records,  Agnes Jackson  married Edward Harmon on Nov. 27, 
1788
,
		 Isreal Jackson married Polly Handsor on Aug. 29, 
1802
,
		Hester Jackson  married Eli Hitchins on Sept. 9, 
1802
,
		 and   Katherine Jackson  married Thomas Hanzor on Feb. 4, 
1808
.

1789
. He also appears in the 
1810
 and 
1820
 census records for Indian River Hundred, listed as "free 			colored" 
  Stephen Jackson  appears in the Indian River taxables from 
1773
 - 
1784
. He's also listed
		in the 
1810
 and 
1820
 Dagsboro Hundred census records as "free colored". 


From this we can say that: 

 John Jackson was the father of William Jackson & Patience Jackson

The recorded marriages to Handsor, Hitchins and Harmon - names that appear among the current mixed raced community- indicates that as early at the mid 18th century Jacksons were a part of the mixed race Indian community in Sussex County, DE.
